subject: Interregional active/passive pools — architecture, failover pricing, and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nomadapps.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nomadapps.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing question and DR options for Dedicated commitment

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the intro. NomadApps is kicking off an evaluation for a multi-region dedicated deployment and we want to understand cost / architecture tradeoffs before we lock a commit. A few high-level asks so we can prepare an internal MA/PO: 

- We plan to serve conversational features from two regions (us-west and us-east). We'd prefer an active/passive pattern to keep costs down, but need a clear failover SLA.
- Our peak workload target is ~2,000 tokens/sec (aggregate) with spiky bursts. Can you map that to the GPU pool sizing you recommend and the throughput guarantees you can commit to (99p latency targets)?
- How do you price replication / warm-standby pools? Specifically: are warm-standby replicas billed at full commit levels or at a discounted standby rate?
- If we sign a reserved commit across two regions, do you offer credits for the secondary/replica region? What's typical for a 12/24 month term?

Attached is the preliminary SOW NomadApps uses (NomadApps_SOW_v1.pdf). Appreciate a short write-up + an example pricing sheet we can send to procurement.

Goal: confirm approach and get a commercial outline this week so procurement can prep a PO.

Best,
Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Platform, NomadApps
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nomadapps.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nomadapps.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing question and DR options for Dedicated commitment

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear brief and the SOW. Quick summary of options and what they mean for cost and SLAs: 

1) Active/passive (recommended for cost-sensitive customers)
- Primary region: full committed pool sized for your peak. Secondary: warm-standby configured to receive KV/cache replication and can be scaled or promoted on failover.
- Billing model: Primary billed at committed rate. Warm-standby eligible for a standby credit (we typically offer a 20-30% credit off the equivalent committed price depending on term and whether KV cache replication is enabled).
- Failover: we provide automated failover with health-checking; expected RTO is typically 2–6 minutes, but KV cache warmup means some sessions may see cold starts for X tokens depending on recent traffic patterns. We can negotiate a shorter RTO with pre-warmed replicas (cost increases).

2) Active/active (higher availability, higher cost)
- Both regions actively serve traffic; you get lower failover impact but pay near full committed rates for both pools. Typically chosen when strict <30s failover is required.

Throughput sizing guidance (very high level):
- 2,000 tokens/sec aggregate: approximately 16–24 vGPU units at 512-token context for steady throughput (depends on model family and quantization). We'll run a short perf test on your traffic profile to refine.
- 99th percentile latency SLO mapping: for a tuned config we target 99p generation latency under 250ms for single-request workloads at that throughput; tighter SLOs are possible with higher provisioning and reserved CPU/RAM for pre/post processing.

Commercials / next steps: I attached a preliminary pricing sheet. Rishi will follow with more granular pricing by commit/term. If you want a phased approach (start with single-region commit + warm-standby) we can show the ramp economics.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the numbers.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nomadapps.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nomadapps.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing question and DR options for Dedicated commitment

Hi Maya — following on Evelyn's note with concrete commercial alternatives and illustrative numbers. These are preliminary and will be formalized in a revised SOW once we agree architecture and term.

Assumptions:
- Workload: 2k tokens/sec peak, model family = mid-sized LLM (~15B), typical seq len 512.
- vGPU unit = approximate serving capacity equivalent to a single A100-80GB class shard.

Option A — Single-region commit + warm-standby (active/passive)
- Primary commit: 20 vGPU units (steady-state buffer for spikes). Base list: $120k/month.
- Warm-standby (cold-warm mirror in secondary region): billable at 40% of full committed price by default.
- Effective monthly outlay (baseline): $120k + $48k = $168k/month.
- Discounting: 12-month term = 10% off list; 24-month = 18%; 36-month = 25% (applied to combined committed base; standby credit applied before % discount).

Option B — Dual-region active/active (both regions actively serving)
- 2x full commit (20 vGPU each): list $240k/month.
- Discounts: same tiering as above but applied per-region. No standby credit since both are active.

Replication / standby credit note
- Our standard standby credit is 40% off equivalent committed price for warm-standby configured with KV replication and automated promotion. For customers committing >$1.5M ARR we can expand that to 50% subject to a 24+ month term.

Cross-region routing and egress
- Cross-region routing for failover is included in platform control plane. Data egress (model payloads and KV sync) is billed at cost-recovery; estimate ~2–3% of committed spend for typical chat workloads.

SLA & throughput guarantees
- We can offer a throughput guarantee mapped to a commit size: e.g., 20 vGPU commit => committed throughput 2,200 tokens/sec with a 99th percentile tail latency target of 300ms for single-request paths.
- SLA credits: 5% credit on monthly bill per missed SLO up to a max of 50% per month (standard enterprise schedule). Exact SLA language goes into MSA.

Overage / bursting
- We support burst capacity beyond commit at metered overage rates. For committed customers we offer pre-negotiated burst caps and a discounted overage rate (typically 60% of list on incremental units for the month).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm target term (12/24/36) and whether you want standby credit negotiated to 50% for a 24+ month commit.
2) Agree on desired RTO target (we quoted 2–6 min standard; can reduce to <2 min with pre-warmed replicas but increases standby effective cost).
3) We'll produce a revised SOW + formal pricing spreadsheet and a PO-ready quote.

Attaching the "redwood-tilt-pricing-sheet.xlsx" with line-item math.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nomadapps.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nomadapps.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing question and DR options for Dedicated commitment

Maya — quickly adding operational/technical constraints to the commercial options so expectations are aligned: 

- Failover behavior: our automated failover promotes the secondary pool and re-routes traffic via the control plane. For active/passive you should expect a 2–6 minute propagation window for DNS + LB updates. If you want sub-30s switchovers we need active-active with health-based routing and sticky session designs.

- KV cache warming: warm-standby keeps KV replication in near real-time, but the in-memory KV cache on GPUs will be cold until warmed by traffic. We recommend a short pre-warm runbook (we can pre-populate hot prefixes) to reduce cold-start exposure for high-priority flows.

- Routing policy: define route-by-latency vs route-by-cost. We can implement an adaptive policy that keeps preferred traffic local and routes overflow to the replica depending on latency thresholds. Cross-region routing for overflow incurs the egress estimate Rishi called out.

Mutual action plan (proposal):
1) Week 0: Sign NDAs/MSA + provide SOW acceptance.
2) Week 1–2: Performance test on a representative sample; finalize vGPU sizing.
3) Week 3: Provide PO and lock commit.
4) Week 4–6: Provision primary + standby, run pre-warm scripts, run failover drills.

I'll sync with your infra owner (Liam) on the test dataset and timings.

- Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@nomadapps.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nomadapps.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing question and DR options for Dedicated commitment

Thanks all — helpful and detailed. A few follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Commercial preference: NomadApps prefers a phased commit. Proposed: 6-month evaluation single-region commit (12 vGPU) with warm-standby mirror in us-east billed at a 30% standby credit. After 6 months we ramp to the full 20 vGPU commit and extend to a 24-month term. Please model the economics for that ramp and send a revised SOW reflecting the phased term.

- Standby credit: Rishi noted standard 40% (and 50% for >$1.5M ARR). Procurement counters with 15% standby credit for our initial phase — we will push to 30% once we commit to 24 months. Can you show both scenarios in the spreadsheet?

- RTO/RPO: we need a 2-hour RPO for critical customer sessions and a 2-hour RTO in contract for the initial phase. If you can meet a 2-hour RTO at the phased price point that makes the initial commit more palatable. If <2 hours requires pre-warming and higher standby cost, outline that specifically.

- Timing: Procurement aims to issue a PO within 3 weeks of receiving the revised SOW (target PO date: 11 Apr 2027). We'll need DocuSign-ready commercial terms and the hubspot deal updated to reflect the phased approach.

Please include the SOW and the pricing workbook with both the 15% and 30/40% standby credit scenarios. We'll set a short call early next week to finalize.

Best,
Maya
